docs.title: Every efficient attention method changes one object in one formula
docs.text:
attnbank v0.2.0 · 32 methods · one invariant · 1254 tests

Attention is a query-conditioned expectation. Efficiency has to come from somewhere, and there are only so many places it can come from: a method either evaluates the expectation differently, or it changes one of the objects in it. There are seven objects, so there are seven categories — and that is the library's directory structure, not a diagram drawn afterwards.

y(q)=∫v dπq πq=g(q, ·)μZ(q)

Ht = Ht−1 + ψ(kt) vt⊤ — a different operator, not an approximation

Seven keys, one per object a method can change. Choosing one shows where that category reaches into the operator.

Changes Nothing. The integrand, the measure and the normaliser are the reference operator's; only the order of the arithmetic changes. Consequence Tiling, online softmax and partitioned reductions reassociate the same sum, so the answer is identical and only the memory traffic moves. The interesting question is where exactness stops — flash and splitk are exact to floating point, lowprec is not, and that boundary is the point of the category. Read on exact in the taxonomy Changes The interaction g(q, x), replaced by a cheaper surrogate ĝ on the same n positions. Consequence Separable surrogates turn the numerator and the normaliser into finite moments. The values are untouched, so the whole error is distributional. Positive features keep π̂q a probability measure; trigonometric and Nyström ones do not, and say so in an attribute rather than in a footnote. Read on interaction in the taxonomy Changes The support of πq, which shrinks to a subset Sq and is renormalised on it. Consequence One operator, differing only in how Sq is chosen — and the error has an exact closed form: the omitted mass times the contrast between the omitted and the retained conditional means. Nothing is discarded, so the context stays available to later queries. Read on restrict in the taxonomy Changes The stored context (μ, k, v) itself — quantised, factored, evicted, merged, or shared across heads. Consequence The only category that routinely perturbs the integrand, so v̂ ≠ v and the error has a value term as well as a distributional one. Key error passes through the softmax; value error is only reweighted, which is why keys cost more per bit. Read on compress in the taxonomy Changes The shape of πq: it is routed through r latents, πq = a(q, ·) b(·, x), which caps the rank of the attention matrix at r. Consequence A composition of two Markov kernels is still a probability measure, so normalisation survives. The price is structural: nonnegative rank exceeds rank, so a stochastic factorisation cannot reach a signed one of the same size — and the bank carries both oracles that measure the gap. Read on factorize in the taxonomy Changes The normalisation. Z(q) stops being a per-query constant and becomes a global constraint. Consequence Imposing marginals on the joint law couples queries that softmax treats independently, and the conditionals that come back are exactly softmax tilted by one potential per key. Queries are no longer independent, so there is no causal version — and asking for one raises an error that says so. Read on coupling in the taxonomy Changes The operator. y comes from a finite-state recurrence over positions rather than from an integral against a measure. Consequence A fixed-size state must serve every future query, which bounds recall however it is trained. It is still linear in v, so the invariant holds and the implied weights can be written down — they are simply not a probability measure. Fidelity to softmax is not the goal here. Read on recurrent in the taxonomy

A second axis cuts across all seven, and it decides how a method should be judged at all: an approximate method targets dense softmax and is fairly measured by output error; a modify method is a different operator, and fidelity to softmax was never its goal. Conflating the two is the most persistent confusion in this literature, so every method here declares which it is — and the test suite reads the declaration.

docs.title: One invariant, held by all 32
docs.text:
Every method realises, explicitly or implicitly, a measure \(\widehat\pi_q\) over context positions and a value field \(\widehat v\) — and must be able to hand you both.

y == weights @ (v_hat if v_hat is not None else value)

Checked for every registered method, in float32 and float64.

This is the load-bearing property of the library. The error metrics decompose output error into a distributional term and a value term, and that decomposition is meaningless unless each method's reported weights and values really do reproduce its own output. A method that genuinely cannot express its measure on the original \(n\) positions declares expresses_weights = False and is excluded from those studies by declaration, not by accident.

Correctness is anchored to an exact limit rather than to inspection. Each method declares the configuration under which it provably reduces to dense softmax — top-\(k\) with \(k = n\), quantisation at full precision, Nyström with every token a landmark — and the suite holds it to that, to 1e-5 in the output and 1e-6 in the weights. There is nowhere for a transposed index or a dropped scale factor to hide.

the conformance suite, parametrised over every registered method

  1. Shapes, for every tensor the method returns
  2. The invariant above
  3. Row stochasticity, where the method claims it
  4. No causal leakage, under perturbation of future keys
  5. Batch and head independence
  6. Exact reduction to softmax at the declared limit
  7. Monotone convergence, for the Monte-Carlo estimators
  8. Agreement across float32, float64, CPU and CUDA
  9. A cost model that is finite, positive and consistent
  10. No NaN at empty support or at large logits
  11. Every cited key resolves in the bibliography

A method that cannot pass a check must say so in a declaration attribute, not in a skip. How the suite reads those declarations.

docs.title: What the approximation cost you, and in which of the two ways
docs.text:
import attnbank as ab

rows = ab.compare(["softmax", "topk", "performer", "quantkv"], query, key, value,
                  configs={"topk": {"k": 16}, "performer": {"r": 64},
                           "quantkv": {"bits_k": 16, "bits_v": 2}})
output error distributional value topk 1.03 1.03 0.00 performer 2.76 2.76 0.00 quantkv 0.72 0.00 0.72

Restriction moves mass to the wrong places. Quantisation aggregates the wrong values. Both arrive as "error" in a single number; only the split says which mechanism is at fault — and the split is algebra, not a heuristic. It closes to \(8.5\times10^{-15}\) over 1.78 million query rows.

docs.title: Five minutes
docs.text:
pip install attnbank

import attnbank as ab

y = ab.attend("topk", query, key, value, causal=True, k=64)

Tensors are [B, H, n, d] throughout, and causal masking aligns the last query with the last key, so the same code path serves prefill and decode.

The taxonomy The seven categories as a tree you can open, with what each one preserves and which error term it incurs. Browse the bank All 32 methods, searchable by name, category, objective, backend and flag — one generated page each. The invariant Why weights @ v_hat is the property everything else rests on, and what it costs a method to be unable to supply it. Backends reference, sdpa, flash_attn, and why most of the bank correctly declares only the first. Examples gallery Ten short scripts, each executed to produce the output shown beside it. API reference Every public function, with a runnable example in its docstring.

docs.title: Citing
docs.text:
attnbank is the companion code for What Does Efficient Attention Approximate? A Unified View of Interactions, Memory, and Error. If the library or its taxonomy is useful in your work, please cite the monograph:

@article{shahbazi2026attention,
  title  = {What Does Efficient Attention Approximate?
            A Unified View of Interactions, Memory, and Error},
  author = {Shahbazi, Ashkan},

docs.title: Backends
docs.text:
A method in this bank is two things that are easy to confuse: an operator — the mathematics, one readable file — and an execution path. The operator never changes with the backend. The execution path does, and you choose it.

print(ab.backends())                    # what runs here, and why anything does not
ab.build("softmax", backend="sdpa")     # ask for one explicitly
ab.backend_matrix()                     # which method declares which

docs.title: The four backends
docs.text:
backend what it is needs reference plain PyTorch; the correctness anchor and the default nothing sdpa torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention; on CUDA this is FlashAttention-2 or the memory-efficient kernel torch ≥ 2.2 flash_attn the flash-attn package CUDA, fp16/bf16, pip install attnbank[flash] xformers, triton detected and reported, declared by nothing —

xformers and triton are listed because silence would be worse. ab.backends() says why neither is used: torch ≥ 2.2 already routes sdpa to the same memory-efficient kernel, so a second path would add a dependency and a second thing to keep equal to the reference; and the bank ships no hand-written Triton kernel, because these implementations exist to be read against the monograph.

docs.title: The matrix
docs.text:
>>> ab.backend_matrix("sdpa")
{'flash': ('reference', 'sdpa'),
 'gqa': ('reference', 'sdpa'),
 'mla': ('reference', 'sdpa'),
 'softmax': ('reference', 'sdpa', 'flash_attn')}
>>> sum(len(b) == 1 for b in ab.backend_matrix().values())
28

Twenty-eight of thirty-two methods declare reference only, and that is the correct answer. sdpa computes exactly \(\mathrm{softmax}(\beta\langle q,k\rangle + \text{mask})\,v\). Four methods in the bank are that, once their own preprocessing is done: softmax, flash, and — after pooling or reconstructing the cache — gqa and mla. The rest are not:

  • topk, blocktopk, lsh_sample and the evictions report the omitted mass \(\varepsilon_q\) in extras, which needs the full score matrix anyway. A kernel that skips materialising it cannot produce it.
  • nmf_oracle and svd_oracle are factorisations; merge_kv is a clustering step; sinkhorn is a fixed-point iteration. None of them is a kernel call.
  • lowprec quantises inside the kernel and returns the perturbed logits.

Declaring sdpa for those would be pretending. ab.describe says so explicitly:

backends     reference   (reference only: no equivalent kernel exists for this operator)

docs.title: Detection explains itself
docs.text:
attnbank backends on this machine (torch 2.10.0+cu128, cuda yes)
----------------------------------------------------------------
reference   available    plain PyTorch; always available; the correctness anchor
            version: 2.10.0+cu128
sdpa        available    torch SDPA; CUDA dispatches to FlashAttention-2 or mem-efficient
            version: 2.10.0+cu128
flash_attn  unavailable  the flash-attn package; CUDA, fp16/bf16 only
            reason: the flash_attn package is not installed
            fix:    pip install 'attnbank[flash]'   # needs CUDA and a C++ toolchain
…
default: 'reference'.

Every unavailable backend carries a reason and, where one exists, the exact command that fixes it.

docs.title: Selection, and why fallback is loud
docs.text:
Three rules:

  1. No backend named. Use the process default if the method supports it and it is installed, otherwise reference. Quiet — a default is a preference.
  2. A backend the method does not declare. Raise BackendNotSupportedError, listing what it does declare. An explicit request is an instruction; silently doing something else would make a benchmark meaningless.
  3. A declared backend that is not installed here. Warn with BackendFallbackWarning and use reference. Announced, never silent.

There is a fourth case inside a call: no fused kernel materialises \(\widehat\pi_q\), so return_weights=True falls back to reference for that call and says so. The result is identical; only the speed is not. (transformers does the same for output_attentions under attn_implementation="sdpa".)

with ab.default_backend("sdpa"):        # process-wide, scoped
    ...
ab.set_default_backend("reference")     # or permanently

docs.title: Pinning the sub-backend
docs.text:
"SDPA" is three kernels with three numerics profiles. For a benchmark, pin one:

ab.build("softmax", backend="sdpa", sdpa_kernel="flash")          # FlashAttention-2
ab.build("softmax", backend="sdpa", sdpa_kernel="mem_efficient")
ab.build("softmax", backend="sdpa", sdpa_kernel="math")

An unavailable sub-backend raises rather than quietly choosing another.

docs.title: One detail worth knowing
docs.text: is_causal=True in SDPA aligns the mask at the top left. This library aligns the last query with the last key, so query i sees 0 … i + (n - m). They agree only when m == n. attnbank.components.sdpa_attend therefore always passes an explicit boolean mask, which makes decode (m < n) correct rather than accidentally right — and tests/test_backends.py asserts that the naive is_causal=True call would in fact disagree, so the test keeps proving something.

docs.title: Equality is tested, not asserted
docs.text: Declaring a backend is a claim, and tests/test_conformance.py::test_backend_equivalence is where it is checked: every method, every declared backend, both causal settings, float32 and float64, on five shapes including m < n, n == 1 and logits scaled by 10. Tolerances are 1e-5 (fp32) and 1e-10 (fp64), scaled by \(\lVert y\rVert_\infty\). On a CUDA machine the same comparison runs again on device, where sdpa dispatches to a genuinely fused kernel.

docs.title: The studies are pinned
docs.text:
Every number in the monograph came out of attnbank/studies/. Importing that package pins the default backend to reference:

# attnbank/studies/__init__.py
from ..backends import REFERENCE, set_default_backend

set_default_backend(REFERENCE)

A published figure must not be able to move because the library grew a faster path. tests/test_backends.py asserts the pin in a subprocess, and separately greps the eight study modules for a backend override.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to attnbank are recorded here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project follows Semantic Versioning.

The one thing that will never change silently is Invariant W (y == weights @ (v_hat or value)). If a release ever relaxes it, that release is a major version and this file says so in the first line.

docs.title: 0.2.0 — 2026-10-22
docs.text: The release that turns the research code into a library. No method's mathematics, no number and no result file changed; everything below is interface, documentation and packaging.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ab.list_methods() — the bank as a readable table grouped by category, with the declaration columns that drive the test suite. Returns a MethodTable, which is a plain list of row dicts that happens to print well, and carries .names and .filter(**constraints).
  • ab.describe(name) — one method in full: what it changes, what it declares, its constructor signature with defaults, its correctness anchor, its paper section and its citations. Also reachable as AttentionMethod.describe().
  • ab.categories() — the taxonomy as {category: what it changes}.
  • ab.check_invariant(output, value) and ab.check_conformance(name, **config) — the design contract as a runtime API, not only as a test file. check_conformance returns a printable report over shapes, Invariant W, row stochasticity, causal non-leakage, finiteness at large logits, input immutability, reproducibility, the cost model and the exact limit.
  • Errors that teach. A new attnbank.errors module. Unknown method names suggest near matches (difflib); shape errors name the argument, what was expected and what arrived; causal=True on a supports_causal = False method explains that this is a statement about the operator and names the methods that do support it; an unrecognised config key is rejected with the accepted keys and a near match, instead of being silently swallowed. Every class subclasses both AttnBankError and the built-in exception a caller would catch, so existing except KeyError / except ValueError handlers keep working.
  • __repr__ everywhere. AttentionOutput shows the shape of each field, the keys in extras, the dtype and the device. AttentionMethod shows its name, category, objective and configuration.
  • Type hints and a py.typed marker, so downstream type checkers see the API.
  • Runnable examples in every public docstring, executed in CI by tests/test_docs.py; a public function without an example now fails the build.
  • An examples gallery (examples/) of short, self-contained scripts, each executed in CI by tests/test_examples.py and rendered as a page of the documentation site.
  • A documentation site (MkDocs + Material + mkdocstrings): quickstart, the taxonomy, the invariant, the conformance suite, the API reference and the gallery.
  • A packaged bibliography (attnbank/references.bib) containing every key cited by a method, so conformance check 11 — "every citation resolves" — survives the split from the monograph's repository.
  • An execution-backend layer. A method is now an operator (one readable file) and an execution path. ab.backends() reports what this machine can run and, for anything it cannot, why and the exact pip install that would fix it; ab.backend_matrix() shows which method declares which; ab.build(name, backend="sdpa") selects one, ab.default_backend(...) scopes a default.
  • Backends: reference (plain PyTorch, always available, the default and the correctness anchor), sdpa (torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention, with sdpa_kernel= to pin the FlashAttention-2 / memory-efficient / math sub-backend), flash_attn (the flash-attn package, CUDA + fp16/bf16). xformers and triton are detected and reported as deliberately unused, with the reason, rather than left to guesswork.
  • Four methods declare a non-reference backend: softmax, flash, gqa, mla. The other twenty-eight declare reference only, which is the correct answer for an operator that is not a dense softmax over a mask — and ab.describe prints the reason rather than a blank.
  • Equivalence is tested, not asserted. tests/test_conformance.py::test_backend_equivalence compares every declared backend against reference for both causal settings, float32 and float64, on m < n, m == n, n == 1, a single decode step and logits scaled by 10, and again on CUDA where available. Tolerances 1e-5 (fp32) and 1e-10 (fp64), scaled by ‖y‖∞.
  • Selection is never silent: an undeclared backend raises BackendNotSupportedError naming what the method does declare; a declared but uninstalled backend warns with BackendFallbackWarning and falls back; and return_weights=True — which no fused kernel can serve — falls back for that call and says so.
  • attnbank/components/ — the behaviour that recurs across methods, in one documented place, so a method file shows what the method adds: the online-softmax monoid (flash, splitk), the quantisers (lowprec, quantkv), the renormalised restriction (every selector in restrict/, both evictions in compress/), the recurrent feature maps and readout, and the shared SDPA call. The old private module paths (methods/restrict/_restriction.py, methods/recurrent/_state.py) remain as re-export shims, so no import broke.
  • tests/test_backends.py — detection, selection, announcement, the matrix, and the study pin.
  • LICENSE (Apache-2.0), CONTRIBUTING.md, this file, and a GitHub Actions workflow running pytest and ruff on Python 3.10–3.13, plus jobs that build the docs strictly, build and twine check the distribution, and verify that a bare pip install attnbank still works with neither matplotlib nor transformers present.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The positional parameters of every forward pass are now query, key, value (the transformers convention) rather than q, k, v. This frees k= to mean what a reader expects: ab.attend("topk", q, k, v, k=64) sets top-k's budget. The tensors remain positional, so every existing call is unaffected; passing a Tensor as q=, k= or v= is still understood, and the old escape spelling k_=64 still works.
  • ab.available() takes an objective= filter alongside category=.
  • pyproject.toml is PyPI-ready: metadata, classifiers, keywords, URLs, and optional extras so the core install is torch and numpy only. Plotting moved to [viz], real-activation capture to [studies], the optional CUDA kernels to [flash] / [triton] / [xformers] / [fast], the docs toolchain to [docs], and everything a contributor needs to [dev].
  • attnbank/studies/ pins backend="reference" on import. Every number in the monograph came out of those modules; a published figure must not be able to move because a faster execution path appeared. tests/test_backends.py asserts the pin in a subprocess and separately greps the eight study modules for an override. No result file was touched and no sweep was re-run.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • Nothing. The trailing-underscore spelling k_= is redundant now that k= works, but it is supported and tested, and no removal is scheduled.
Initial internal release: the taxonomy, thirty-two methods, attnbank.metrics, the eleven-point conformance suite, and the eight studies behind the monograph.

docs.title: The conformance suite
docs.text:
tests/test_conformance.py is parametrized over every registered method and is the reason this library can be trusted. Registering a method is all it takes to be included — there is no second list to update, and no list of exemptions anywhere in the file.

pytest tests/test_conformance.py -q

A method that cannot pass a check must say so in a declaration attribute, not in a skip. The suite then tests it against what it claims. That is the whole design: the attributes in a method's class body are commitments, and this file is where they are collected.

docs.title: The eleven checks
docs.text: check what it rules out 1 shapes y is [B,H,m,dv], weights is [B,H,m,n], v_hat is [B,H,n,dv] 2 Invariant W reported weights that do not reproduce the output 3 row stochasticity a method claiming a probability measure and not delivering one 4 causal leakage perturb k[…, t:, :]; earlier outputs must be bit-for-bit unchanged 5 batch and head independence accidental coupling across the batch or head axis 6 exact limit an implementation that is plausible rather than correct 7 convergence a Monte-Carlo estimator that does not actually converge 8 dtype and device float32 / float64 / CPU / CUDA disagreement 8 (cont.) backend equivalence a kernel that is not the operator it claims to be 9 cost model three keys, finite, positive; capacity savers really save capacity 10 no NaN / no Inf empty support, single-element support, logits scaled by 10 11 references resolve an implementation with no source

docs.title: Why 6 and 7 are the interesting ones
docs.text:
Checks 1–5 catch bugs. Check 6 catches something else: an implementation that is plausible rather than correct.

Every method whose objective is accelerate or approximate declares an anchor — a configuration under which it provably reduces to dense softmax:

TopKAttention.limit_config()      # {'k': None}   — keep every visible key
QuantKVAttention.limit_config()   # {'bits_k': None, 'bits_v': None}
NystromAttention.limit_config()   # {'r': None}   — landmarks = all tokens

The suite builds the method under that configuration and requires it to match softmax to 1e-5 in the output and 1e-6 in the weights. There is nowhere for a transposed index or a dropped scale factor to hide.

Monte-Carlo estimators have no exact limit at finite resource. performer and trigrff declare convergence_configs() instead — a sequence of configurations along which the mean error, over seeds, must decrease monotonically:

errs = [mean_error(cfg) for cfg in cls.convergence_configs()]
assert all(a > b for a, b in zip(errs, errs[1:]))

Methods whose objective is modify are exempt, and the suite asserts the exemption rather than silently skipping it:

def test_has_an_anchor(name):
    cls = ab.get_class(name)
    if cls.objective is Objective.MODIFY:
        return          # a different operator: neither anchor is meaningful
    assert cls.limit_config() is not None or cls.convergence_configs() is not None

linear_elu, cosformer, latent_stochastic, lowrank_ot and the three recurrences neither reduce to nor converge to softmax. That is what it means to define a different operator. Demanding an anchor of them would be demanding that they stop being what they are.

docs.title: Declarations the suite reads
docs.text: attribute what the suite does with it supports_causal runs check 4, or skips it with the declaration as the reason expresses_weights requires weights to be present and absent, correspondingly row_stochastic runs check 3 head_independent gqa and mla share K/V across query heads, so check 5 verifies the coupling boundary instead: head h moves its whole group and nothing outside it. Sharing is the mechanism, not a defect objective decides whether an anchor is required (check 6/7) backends decides which equivalence cases run (check 8) references check 11 resolves every key in attnbank/references.bib

docs.title: Backend equivalence (part of check 8)
docs.text:
Declaring a backend is a claim that it computes the same operator, so the suite checks it: for every method, every declared backend, both causal settings, float32 and float64, and the awkward shapes — m < n, n == 1, a single decode step, and logits scaled by 10.

Tolerances are 1e-5 (fp32) and 1e-10 (fp64), scaled by \(\lVert y\rVert_\infty\) so the number is a statement about precision rather than about the test inputs. A backend that cannot meet them is not declared. See Backends.

docs.title: At runtime
docs.text:
The same contract is available without pytest:

ab.check_invariant(out, value)
ab.check_conformance("topk")           # a printable report
ab.check_conformance("topk", strict=True)   # raises on failure

check_conformance runs the fast half — shapes, Invariant W, row stochasticity, causal non-leakage, finiteness at large logits, input immutability, reproducibility, the cost model and the exact limit. The float64/CUDA matrix, head independence, Monte-Carlo convergence and the bibliography check stay in the test file, where they belong.

docs.title: Rules of thumb the suite exists to enforce
docs.text:
• Compute softmax in log space; never materialise exp of an unshifted score.
  • A fully masked row must produce a documented, finite result — never nan. Window methods guarantee at least one visible key by including the diagonal.
  • Renormalise explicitly, with a floored denominator, and assert in tests that the floor was never reached.
  • Never mutate q, k or v.
  • Seeded randomness goes through torch.Generator, never the global RNG, so studies reproduce and two builds agree bit for bit.

DESIGN.md is the normative version of this page. If an implementation and that file disagree, the file wins.

docs.title: Contributing to attnbank
docs.text:
The library is small on purpose. The useful contribution is almost always a new method, and the bar for one is specific: it must declare what it is, and it must pass the conformance suite on the strength of that declaration. Nothing is merged with a skip.

git clone https://github.com/Ashkan13776/attnbank
cd attnbank
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q          # ~1000 tests, about ten seconds on a laptop
ruff check .

docs.title: 1. Decide what it changes
docs.text:
Every efficient attention method changes exactly one object in

\[y(q) \;=\; \int v \,\mathrm{d}\pi_q, \qquad \pi_q \;=\; \frac{g(q,\cdot)\,\mu}{Z(q)} .\]

That choice is the directory it goes in. ab.categories() prints the seven options; DESIGN.md §3 lists the methods already in each. Do not invent a new category — if a method genuinely does not fit, that is a finding about the taxonomy and belongs in an issue before it belongs in a pull request.

One method per file: attnbank/methods/<category>/<name>.py.

docs.title: 2. Declare what it is
docs.text:
@ab.register
class MyAttention(ab.AttentionMethod):
    name = "my_method"                    # unique, lowercase, no spaces
    category = ab.Category.RESTRICT       # which object it changes
    objective = ab.Objective.APPROXIMATE  # accelerate | approximate | modify
    supports_causal = True
    expresses_weights = True              # can it name pi_hat on the original n?
    row_stochastic = True                 # are those weights a distribution?
    head_independent = True               # False only if it shares K/V across heads
    trainable = False
    references = ("author2024paper",)     # keys that resolve in references.bib
    paper_section = "sec:sparse"
    backends = ("reference",)             # see step 5; this is usually correct

Those attributes are commitments, not documentation. The conformance suite reads them and tests the method against what it claims, which is why there is no list of exemptions anywhere in the suite: a method that cannot be row-stochastic says row_stochastic = False and the check becomes inapplicable rather than skipped.

Two of them deserve care.

  • objective. ACCELERATE means exact up to floating point. APPROXIMATE means the method targets dense softmax and is judged by fidelity to it. MODIFY means it defines a different operator and fidelity to softmax is not its goal. Mislabelling an operator modification as an approximation is the most common mistake in this literature; the library exists partly to make the distinction unavoidable.
  • expresses_weights. Set it to False only if the method genuinely cannot write its measure on the original \(n\) positions. Setting it to False to dodge Invariant W is the one thing that will get a pull request closed: it silently removes the method from every error-decomposition study.

docs.title: 3. Implement three things
docs.text:
def _forward(self, q, k, v, causal, return_weights) -> AttentionOutput: ...
def cost(self, m, n, d, dv, bytes_per_el=2) -> dict:   # flops, state_bytes, bytes_moved
@classmethod
def limit_config(cls) -> dict | None: ...

Inside a method file the maths is written in the paper's q, k, v notation; the public argument names (query, key, value) are the base class's business.

_forward must return an AttentionOutput satisfying

y == weights @ (v_hat if v_hat is not None else v)

in float64 to 1e-10. This is Invariant W and it is the whole point of the library: attnbank.metrics splits output error into a distributional and a value term, and that split is a measurement only if the reported weights and values actually reproduce the output.

limit_config() returns the configuration under which the method provably reduces to dense softmax — {"k": None} for top-k, {"bits": 16} for quantisation — and the suite uses it as a correctness anchor. A Monte-Carlo estimator with no exact limit at finite resource returns None and supplies convergence_configs() instead, a sequence along which the mean error must decrease. Only methods whose objective is MODIFY are exempt, and the suite asserts the exemption rather than skipping it.

Four rules that prevent the bugs we actually hit:

  1. Compute softmax in log space; never materialise exp of an unshifted score.
  2. A fully masked row must produce a documented, finite result — never nan. Window methods guarantee at least one visible key by including the diagonal.
  3. Renormalise explicitly, and floor the denominator: pi / pi.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(TINY).
  4. Seeded randomness goes through torch.Generator, never the global RNG, so studies reproduce and two builds agree bit for bit.

Never mutate q, k or v. That is tested.

docs.title: 4. Wire it up and check
docs.text:
Import the module in the category's __init__.py. That is the only registration step — the conformance suite is parametrized over the registry, so it picks the method up automatically.

import attnbank as ab
print(ab.check_conformance("my_method"))     # the fast half, immediately

(Steps 5 and 6 below are about backends and shared components; step 4 is the only wiring you need to be picked up by the suite.)

pytest tests/test_conformance.py -k my_method    # the full eleven points
pytest -q                                        # and everything else

The eleven checks, in order: shapes · Invariant W · row stochasticity · causal non-leakage · batch and head independence · the exact limit · Monte-Carlo convergence · float32/float64/CUDA agreement · the cost model · no NaN at degenerate supports or large logits · every citation resolves in references.bib. DESIGN.md §4 is the normative description.

docs.title: 5. Declare a backend, or declare reference only
docs.text:
backends = ("reference",)      # the default, and usually the right answer

reference is plain PyTorch: always available, every dtype and device, and the path every other backend is tested against. A method may additionally declare sdpa or flash_attn — but only if it can prove equality. tests/test_conformance.py::test_backend_equivalence compares every declared backend against reference for both causal settings, float32 and float64, on m < n, m == n, n == 1, a single decode step and logits scaled by 10. Tolerances are 1e-5 (fp32) and 1e-10 (fp64), scaled by the output magnitude.

Twenty-eight of the thirty-two methods declare reference only, and they are right to. sdpa computes exactly \(\mathrm{softmax}(\beta\langle q,k\rangle + \text{mask})\,v\); if your operator is not that — or if its extras need the full score matrix anyway, as every score-based selector's omitted mass does — there is nothing to dispatch to. Declaring reference only is a correct answer and far better than pretending otherwise.

If you do declare one, implement _forward_<backend> and route through attnbank.components.sdpa.sdpa_attend rather than calling SDPA directly: it carries the end-alignment convention that is_causal=True gets wrong when m < n. Delegate to self._fallback_to_reference(reason) for anything the kernel cannot serve — return_weights=True, most often — so the fallback is announced rather than silent.

docs.title: 6. Reuse the shared components
docs.text:
Before writing a helper, check attnbank/components/:

module what lives there components.restriction the renormalised restriction of prop:sparse-identity, and topk_support components.online_softmax the state / merge / readout monoid of prop:exact-monoid components.quantization symmetric INT, asymmetric affine with grouping, FP8, Hadamard components.recurrence feature maps and the readout convention components.sdpa the one SDPA call every _forward_sdpa goes through attnbank.core masking, log-space softmax, renormalisation, seeded generators

A new selector in restrict/ should be three lines plus the support rule. If yours is not, either you are reinventing something, or the shared piece needs widening — which is a fine pull request on its own.

docs.title: 7. Add the citation
docs.text: Put the BibTeX entry in attnbank/references.bib. Check 11 fails if a key in references does not resolve there, which is deliberate: an implementation without a source is not reviewable.

docs.title: 8. Write the method's own tests
docs.text: Conformance proves the method is well-formed. It does not prove the method is correct. Add tests/test_<category>.py cases for the behaviour that makes your method what it is — the support it selects, the bound it satisfies, the limit it approaches — the way the existing files do.

docs.title: Other kinds of contribution
docs.text:
A metric. Add it to attnbank/metrics.py with a docstring giving the equation in the paper's notation and a runnable example. A function named *_bound must return an upper bound on something, and tests/test_metrics.py must contain a randomised test that it really bounds it.

Documentation. The site is MkDocs Material; pip install -e ".[docs]" then mkdocs serve. Pages live in docs/, the gallery in examples/.

Two pages are generated and should not be hand-edited:

python docs/gen_taxonomy.py    # docs/taxonomy.md, from the live registry
python docs/gen_gallery.py     # docs/examples/*.md, from examples/*.py + captured output

The gallery pages include each script rather than copying it, so the code can never drift; only the captured output can, which is why the generator re-runs everything. tests/test_examples.py executes every script in CI, so a broken example is a failing build rather than a stale page. mkdocs build --strict runs in CI too: a dangling link is an error.

A docstring. Every public function carries a runnable Examples block, and tests/test_docs.py executes all of them and fails the build for a public name without one. Add the example, run pytest tests/test_docs.py, and paste in the output it tells you it got.

A bug. A failing test first, in the file where the behaviour belongs, then the fix.

docs.title: House style
docs.text:
Reference implementations favour clarity over speed. They are read by people checking the mathematics against the paper with the relevant section open, so: no micro-optimisation, no fused tricks, and no einsum string longer than the equation it implements. Every method file opens with a docstring giving the operator in the paper's notation, the section label and the citation.

ruff check . must be clean; CI runs it on Python 3.10–3.13. Line length is 100.

ruff format is deliberately not enforced. The method files align equations by hand so they can be read next to the monograph, and the formatter would undo that. Match the surrounding file.

docs.title: The contract wins
docs.text: DESIGN.md is the binding specification. If an implementation and that file disagree, the file wins and the implementation is the bug. If you believe the file is wrong, say so in an issue — changing it is a legitimate outcome, changing it quietly in a pull request that also adds a method is not.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: By contributing you agree that your contribution is licensed under the Apache License 2.0, as in LICENSE.

docs.title: Design contract
docs.text:
This page is the binding specification

If an implementation and this file disagree, this file wins and the implementation is the bug. It is reproduced here verbatim from DESIGN.md in the repository root.

docs.title: attnbank design contract
docs.text:
This file is the specification that every method, test and study in attnbank must satisfy. It exists so that the library stays small, predictable and provably consistent with the paper. If an implementation and this file disagree, this file wins — fix the implementation.

Companion to What Does Efficient Attention Approximate? The taxonomy below is the one in sections/03f_comparative.tex (tab:comparative). Do not invent new categories.

docs.title: 1. The one invariant
docs.text:
Every method realises, exactly or implicitly, a measure \(\widehat\pi_q\) over context positions and a value field \(\widehat v\):

\[\widehat y(q) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{n} \widehat\pi_q(j)\,\widehat v_j .\]

Invariant W. If a method returns weights and v_hat, then

y  ==  weights @ (v_hat if v_hat is not None else v)      # within 1e-5 (fp32) / 1e-10 (fp64)

This is checked for every registered method by the conformance suite. It is the single most important property in the library: all of attnbank.metrics presumes it, and every study that decomposes error into a distributional and a value term is meaningless without it.

A method that cannot express its measure on the original \(n\) positions sets expresses_weights = False and returns weights=None. It is then excluded from the decomposition studies, by design, not by accident.

docs.title: 2. Public API (keep it this small)
docs.text:
import attnbank as ab

# --- do something -------------------------------------------------------
ab.attend("topk", query, key, value, causal=True, k=64)   # one-liner: returns y only
ab.build("topk", k=64)                                    # -> AttentionMethod (nn.Module)
ab.compare(["softmax", "topk", "performer"], query, key, value, causal=True)
                                      # -> list[dict] of metrics vs. the reference

out = ab.build("topk", k=64)(query, key, value, causal=True, return_weights=True)
out.y, out.weights, out.v_hat, out.extras

# --- find something -----------------------------------------------------
ab.available()                        # -> ['blocktopk', 'clustered', 'cosformer', ...]
ab.available("restrict", objective="approximate")
ab.list_methods()                     # a readable table grouped by category
ab.describe("topk")                   # one method, in full
ab.categories()                       # {category: what it changes}
ab.method_table()                     # one machine-readable row per method (Appendix C)

# --- check something ----------------------------------------------------
ab.check_invariant(out, value)        # Invariant W; returns the max deviation
ab.check_conformance("topk")          # a printable pass/fail report

# --- choose an execution path -------------------------------------------
ab.backends()                         # what runs here, and why anything does not
ab.backend_matrix()                   # {method: declared backends}
ab.build("softmax", backend="sdpa")
ab.set_default_backend("reference")   # the default; the studies pin it

Tensors: query [B,H,m,d], key [B,H,n,d], value [B,H,n,dv]. Causal masking aligns the last query with the last key, so m <= n and query \(i\) sees keys \(0 \dots i+(n-m)\). This matches decoding.

Naming. The public positional parameters are query, key, value (the transformers convention). They are positional, so attn(q, k, v) is unchanged, and this is what frees k= to mean a method's own budget: ab.attend("topk", q, k, v, k=64). Inside a method file the maths stays in the paper's q, k, v notation. A Tensor passed as q=, k= or v= is still understood as the tensor, and the historical escape spelling k_=64 still works.

AttentionOutput fields are exactly: y, weights, v_hat, extras. Nothing else.

Errors are part of the API. An unknown method name suggests near matches; a wrong shape names the argument, what was expected and what arrived; causal=True on a supports_causal = False method explains that this is a statement about the operator and names the methods that do support it; an unrecognised config key is rejected with the accepted keys. Every class in attnbank.errors subclasses both AttnBankError and the built-in exception a caller would catch.

docs.title: Class attributes a method must declare
docs.text: Attribute Meaning name unique registry key, lowercase, no spaces category Category.{EXACT,INTERACTION,RESTRICT,COMPRESS,FACTORIZE,COUPLING,RECURRENT} objective Objective.{ACCELERATE,APPROXIMATE,MODIFY} — the paper's third axis supports_causal bool expresses_weights bool — can it return \(\widehat\pi_q\) on the original \(n\) positions? row_stochastic bool — are those weights nonnegative and summing to 1? (False for Nyström, Linformer, unnormalized recurrences) trainable bool — are the parameters meaningful only after training? references tuple of BibTeX keys that exist in references.bib paper_section the \label of the section that discusses it, e.g. "sec:sparse" backends execution paths claimed equal to reference; ("reference",) is the correct and common answer

docs.title: Methods a method must implement
docs.text:
def _forward(self, q, k, v, causal, return_weights) -> AttentionOutput: ...
def cost(self, m, n, d, dv, bytes_per_el=2) -> dict:   # 'flops', 'state_bytes', 'bytes_moved'
@classmethod
def limit_config(cls) -> dict | None:
    """Config under which this method provably reduces to dense softmax, or None.
    e.g. TopK -> {'k': None} (all keys); Quantize -> {'bits': 16}.
    The conformance suite uses it as the correctness anchor."""

limit_config is not optional decoration — it is how we show a method is implemented correctly rather than merely plausibly. Every method whose objective is ACCELERATE or APPROXIMATE must declare an anchor: either an exact limit_config(), or — for Monte-Carlo estimators such as performer and trigrff, where no finite r reproduces softmax to tolerance — a convergence_configs() sequence whose error must decrease monotonically toward softmax.

Methods whose objective is MODIFY are exempt, and the suite asserts the exemption rather than silently skipping it. linear_elu, cosformer, latent_stochastic, lowrank_ot, linear_rnn, decay_rnn and delta_rnn neither reduce to nor converge to softmax; that is what it means to define a different operator (tab:comparative, "mod."). Demanding an anchor of them would be demanding that they stop being what they are.

docs.title: 4. Correctness: the conformance suite
docs.text:
tests/test_conformance.py is parametrized over every registered method and is the reason this library can be trusted. Each method must pass, with no exemptions outside the declared attributes:

  1. shapes — y is [B,H,m,dv]; weights (if any) is [B,H,m,n]; v_hat (if any) is [B,H,n,dv].
  2. Invariant W — y == weights @ (v_hat or v).
  3. row stochasticity — if row_stochastic, weights are \(\ge 0\) and rows sum to 1.
  4. causal leakage — perturb k[..., t:, :] and v[..., t:, :]; outputs at query positions before \(t\) must be bit-for-bit unchanged. Run for several \(t\).
  5. batch and head independence — perturbing batch \(b\) or head \(h\) changes nothing elsewhere. Methods that share K/V across query heads (gqa, mla) declare head_independent = False; for them the suite checks the exact coupling boundary instead — perturbing head \(h\) moves its whole group and nothing outside it. Sharing across heads is the mechanism, not a defect.
  6. exact limit — under limit_config(), y matches softmax to 1e-5 (fp32) and the weights match to 1e-6.
  7. convergence — for Monte-Carlo methods, error decreases monotonically (in the mean over seeds) along convergence_configs().
  8. dtype, device and backend — runs in fp32 and fp64 on CPU, and on CUDA when available; fp64 results agree with fp32 within the fp32 tolerance. And, for every backend the method declares in backends, the output matches the reference backend to 1e-5 (fp32) / 1e-10 (fp64) scaled by \(\lVert y\rVert_\infty\) — causal and non-causal, on m < n, m == n, n == 1, a single decode step, and logits scaled by 10, and again on CUDA where available. Declaring a backend is a claim, and this is where it is checked; a backend that cannot meet tolerance is fixed or not declared (Sec. 7).
  9. cost model — cost() returns the three keys, all finite and positive, and state_bytes is \(\le\) the dense softmax value for any method claiming to save capacity.
  10. no NaN / no Inf anywhere in the output, including for rows with empty or single-element support, and for inputs with large logits (q,k scaled by 10).
  11. references exist — every key in references is present in references.bib.

Rules of thumb that prevent the bugs we care about:

  • Compute softmax in log-space; never materialise exp of an unshifted score.
  • A fully masked row must produce a documented, finite result — never nan. Window methods must guarantee at least one visible key (include the diagonal).
  • Renormalise explicitly: pi = pi / pi.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(tiny) and assert the denominator was not clamped in tests.
  • Never use in-place ops on inputs. Methods must not mutate q, k, v (tested).
  • Seeded randomness goes through torch.Generator, never the global RNG, so studies reproduce.

docs.title: 5. Repository layout
docs.text:
attnbank/
  attnbank/
    core.py registry.py reference.py metrics.py
    errors.py                           # exceptions that say what to do next
    info.py                             # MethodInfo / MethodTable (discoverability)
    conformance.py                      # the contract as a runtime API
    backends.py                         # detection, selection, announced fallback
    components/                         # behaviour shared across methods:
      masking (via core) online_softmax quantization restriction recurrence sdpa
    methods/<category>/<name>.py        # one method per file
    plotting/style.py
    data.py                             # real-activation capture (GPT-2 / Qwen2.5-0.5B)
    studies/__init__.py                 # pins backend="reference" (see Sec. 7)
    studies/_harness.py                 # sweep runner, caching, result tables
    studies/<Sn>_<tag>.py               # one study per file (see STUDIES.md)
    references.bib                      # every key a method cites (check 11)
    py.typed
  tests/test_core.py test_metrics.py test_conformance.py test_backends.py
  tests/test_docs.py test_examples.py test_<category>.py
  examples/<nn>_<tag>.py                # the gallery; executed in CI
  docs/                                 # mkdocs-material site
  results/<study>.json                  # numeric results, committed
figures/<name>.pdf                      # committed, included by the LaTeX sections

One method per file, always. Behaviour that recurs across methods goes in components/ rather than being repeated, so a method file shows what the method adds: flash and splitk share the online-softmax monoid, lowprec and quantkv share the quantisers, every selector in restrict/ and both evictions in compress/ share the renormalised restriction, and every _forward_sdpa shares one SDPA call.

Results are committed as JSON so that every number in the paper can be traced to a file, and so the polish pass can check prose against data without re-running anything.

docs.title: 6. Style
docs.text:
Reference implementations favour clarity over speed; they are read by people checking the maths against the paper. Every method file opens with a docstring giving the operator in the paper's notation, the section label, and the citation. No micro-optimisation, no fused tricks, no einsum strings longer than the equation they implement.

Every public function carries a runnable Examples block. tests/test_docs.py executes all of them and fails the build for a public name without one, so the documentation cannot rot quietly. The same holds for examples/: tests/test_examples.py runs every script.

docs.title: 7. Execution backends
docs.text:
A method is an operator and an execution path. The operator is the file; the execution path is chosen at build time and never changes the operator.

reference    plain PyTorch, always available, every dtype and device. THE DEFAULT and the
             anchor every other backend is tested against.
sdpa         torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention; on CUDA this dispatches to
             FlashAttention-2 or the memory-efficient kernel. `sdpa_kernel=` pins the choice.
flash_attn   the flash-attn package. CUDA, fp16/bf16.
xformers     detected and REPORTED, declared by nothing: torch >= 2.2 already routes `sdpa`
triton       to the same kernels, and the bank ships no hand-written kernel (Sec. 6).

Rules:

  1. A method declares in backends only what it can prove equal to reference (check 8b). ("reference",) is the right answer for an operator that is not a dense softmax over a mask, or whose extras need the full score matrix anyway. Twenty-eight of thirty-two say exactly that, and ab.describe prints the reason rather than leaving a blank.
  2. Selection is explicit. An undeclared backend raises; a declared-but-uninstalled backend warns and falls back to reference. There is no silent downgrade, because a silent downgrade makes a benchmark meaningless.
  3. No fused kernel materialises \(\widehat\pi_q\), so return_weights=True falls back for that call, and says so.
  4. The studies pin reference. attnbank/studies/__init__.py calls set_default_backend("reference") on import. Every number in the paper came out of those modules and must not be able to move because a faster path appeared. tests/test_backends.py asserts the pin in a subprocess and greps the eight study modules for an override.

docs.title: Invariant W
docs.text:
y == weights @ (v_hat if v_hat is not None else value)

Every registered method satisfies this, in float32 and float64, causal and non-causal, on every shape the conformance suite throws at it. It is the single most important property in the library, and the reason the library exists in the form it does.

docs.title: What it says
docs.text:
Every efficient attention method, whatever else it does, realises a measure \(\widehat\pi_q\) over the \(n\) context positions and a value field \(\widehat v\):

\[\widehat y(q) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{n} \widehat\pi_q(j)\,\widehat v_j .\]

Methods do not usually advertise this. A Performer computes feature maps, a StreamingLLM evicts tokens, a linear RNN carries a state matrix. None of them looks like a weighted average over positions. All of them are one, and the library requires each to show you which one.

out = ab.build("performer", r=64)(query, key, value, return_weights=True)
out.weights          # the measure the Performer is implicitly using
ab.check_invariant(out, value)
# 0.0

docs.title: Why it matters
docs.text:
Because of this:

\[y - \widehat y \;=\; \underbrace{(\pi - \widehat\pi)\,v}_{\text{distributional}} \;+\; \underbrace{\widehat\pi\,(v - \widehat v)}_{\text{value}}\]

An approximation can be wrong in exactly two ways — it attends to the wrong places, or it aggregates the wrong values — and this identity separates them exactly, not approximately.

from attnbank import build, metrics

ref = build("softmax")(q, k, v, causal=True, return_weights=True)
out = build("quantkv", bits_k=4, bits_v=4)(q, k, v, causal=True, return_weights=True)
metrics.error_decomposition(ref.weights, out.weights, v, out.v_hat)
# {'distributional': …, 'value': …, 'total': …}

The decomposition is a measurement only if out.weights and out.v_hat really reproduce out.y. If a method reports weights that are merely plausible — the attention matrix it would have used, say, before some later correction — the decomposition becomes a story about a computation that did not happen. Every study in the monograph that separates distributional from value error rests on this, so the library tests it rather than assuming it.

It also pins down something softer: it forces a method to say what it is in a common language. Two methods from different categories, with nothing in common at the level of code, become comparable the moment both can write down \(\widehat\pi_q\) and \(\widehat v\).

docs.title: When a method genuinely cannot
docs.text:
Some methods cannot express their measure on the original \(n\) positions. They declare

expresses_weights = False

and return weights=None. They are then excluded from the decomposition studies by declaration, not by accident — and the conformance suite checks the declaration in both directions:

if not method.expresses_weights:
    assert out.weights is None    # declared False, so it had better not return any
else:
    assert out.weights is not None
    assert torch.allclose(out.y, out.weights @ (out.v_hat or v), atol=1e-9)

Setting the flag to False to dodge the invariant is the one thing that will get a contribution rejected. It silently removes a method from every study that would have measured it.

docs.title: Checking it yourself
docs.text:
ab.check_invariant(output, value)        # -> max |y - weights @ v_hat|, raises if too large
ab.check_conformance("topk")             # -> a printable report including this check

topk: 9 checks passed, 0 failed
  [pass] shapes -- AttentionOutput(y=[2, 2, 6, 6], weights=[2, 2, 6, 12], …)
  [pass] invariant W -- max |y - W v| = 0.00e+00
  [pass] row stochastic -- row sums in [1.000000, 1.000000]
  [pass] no causal leakage -- queries 0..3 unchanged
  [pass] finite at large logits -- q, k scaled by 10
  [pass] inputs not mutated
  [pass] reproducible -- two builds agree bit for bit
  [pass] cost model -- {'flops': 1800, 'state_bytes': 336, 'bytes_moved': 936}
  [pass] exact limit -- limit_config={'k': None}, max |y - softmax| = 4.44e-16

Tolerances: 1e-10 in float64, 1e-5 in float32. The suite runs the check in float64, where there is nowhere for an error to hide.

See the full gallery entry: Invariant W across the whole bank.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
pip install attnbank            # torch + numpy, nothing else

Optional extras, none of them needed to start:

extra what it adds attnbank[viz] matplotlib and the figure style used by the monograph attnbank[fast] flash-attn, triton, xformers — CUDA-only kernels attnbank[studies] transformers + datasets, for capturing real activations attnbank[dev] pytest, ruff and the docs toolchain

docs.title: Tensors
docs.text:
query  [B, H, m, d]
key    [B, H, n, d]
value  [B, H, n, dv]

Causal masking aligns the last query with the last key, so m <= n and query i sees keys 0 … i + (n - m). That is the decode convention, and it means the same code path serves prefill (m == n) and a single decode step (m == 1).

Why query, key, value and not q, k, v

The positional names follow the transformers convention, which frees k= to mean what a reader expects — ab.attend("topk", q, k, v, k=64) is top-k's budget. The tensors are positional, so nothing about attn(q, k, v) changed.

docs.title: attend — the one-liner
docs.text:
import attnbank as ab

y = ab.attend("topk", query, key, value, causal=True, k=64)

Builds the method, runs it, returns y. Nothing else.

docs.title: build — the object
docs.text:
attn = ab.build("topk", k=64)            # a torch.nn.Module
out = attn(query, key, value, causal=True, return_weights=True)

out.y                                     # [B, H, m, dv]
out.weights                               # [B, H, m, n] — the implied measure
out.v_hat                                 # [B, H, n, dv] — if values were compressed
out.extras                                # method-specific diagnostics

return_weights materialises an m × n tensor, so it is off by default.

docs.title: compare — the numbers
docs.text:
rows = ab.compare(["softmax", "topk", "performer"], query, key, value, causal=True,
                  configs={"topk": {"k": 64}, "performer": {"r": 256}})

One JSON-serialisable dict per method: output_error, relative_error, the two terms of the error decomposition, total variation, and the matrix norms of §4.2 — all reduced to a median over queries, batch and heads. Pass raw=True to keep the per-query tensors.

docs.title: Finding a method
docs.text:
ab.list_methods()                 # the whole bank, grouped by category
ab.list_methods("restrict")       # one category
ab.list_methods(causal=True).filter(row_stochastic=True)
ab.available(objective="modify")  # just the names
ab.describe("nystrom")            # one method, in full
ab.categories()                   # what each category means

ab.describe prints the declaration attributes, the constructor signature with its defaults, the correctness anchor, the backends, the paper section and the citations:

=====================================

ab.build("softmax", backend="sdpa")       # PyTorch's fused kernel
ab.backend_matrix()                       # method -> declared backends

The default is reference: plain PyTorch, always available, and the path every other backend is tested against. See Backends.

docs.title: The taxonomy
docs.text:
Attention is a query-conditioned expectation. Efficiency has to come from somewhere, and there are only so many places it can come from: a method either evaluates the expectation differently, or it changes one of the objects in it. Seven categories, because there are seven objects to change.

Open a branch to see what that category changes, what it leaves alone, which term of the error it incurs, and which methods are in it — and which symbol of the operator it reaches for.

y(q)=∫v dπq πq=g(q, ·)μZ(q)

Ht = Ht−1 + ψ(kt) vt⊤ — a different operator, not an approximation

docs.title: exact changes nothing but the order of the arithmetic4 methods
docs.text:
Changes Nothing changes but the evaluation: tiling, chunking, precision. Preserves Everything. The measure, the values and the normaliser are the reference operator's, bit for bit where the arithmetic allows it. Error term None, up to floating point — which is a claim the conformance suite checks rather than a promise. lowprec is the exception, and locating the exception is the purpose of the category. Methods
  • flash
  • lowprec
  • softmax
  • splitk

Nothing in the formula changes — only how it is evaluated. Tiling, chunking, reduced precision. The interesting question in this category is where exactness stops: flash and splitk are exact up to floating point, lowprec is not, and the boundary between them is the point.

docs.title: interaction changes the interaction g5 methods
docs.text:
Changes The interaction g(q, x) is replaced by a cheaper surrogate. Preserves The support, the values, and per-query normalisation — π̂q still lives on all n positions. Error term Distributional only. v̂ = v, so every bit of the error is in the measure. For random features it shrinks with the feature count; for a fixed feature map it does not shrink at all, because there is nothing it is converging to. Methods
  • cosformer
  • linear_elu
  • nystrom
  • performer
  • trigrff

The interaction g(q, x) is replaced by a cheaper surrogate ĝ. Random features estimate exp ⟨q, k⟩; fixed feature maps replace it outright. The first is an approximation whose error shrinks with the feature count; the second is a different operator that happens to be cheap. The objective column is where that difference is recorded.

docs.title: restrict changes the support of πq6 methods
docs.text:
Changes The support of πq is restricted to a subset Sq of positions. Preserves The values and the scores of everything retained. Nothing is discarded from the context, so a later query may select what this one dropped. Error term Distributional only, and in closed form: the omitted mass εq times the contrast between the omitted and the retained conditional means. Minimising εq is not the same as minimising the error, which is what value_topk exists to show. Methods
  • blocktopk
  • lsh_sample
  • sink_window
  • topk
  • value_topk
  • window

The support of πq shrinks to a subset Sq, and the retained mass is renormalised. The whole category is one operator — prop:sparse-identity — differing only in how Sq is chosen. Error is purely distributional: the values are untouched.

docs.title: compress changes the stored context (μ, k, v)8 methods
docs.text:
Changes The stored context (μ, k, v) is replaced by a smaller one. Preserves The operator and the per-query normalisation. What is no longer preserved is the context itself, which is the point. Error term Both. A distributional term through the keys and a value term through v̂ ≠ v — the only category that routinely produces the second. Key error passes through the softmax; value error is only reweighted, so keys cost more per bit. Methods
  • evict_h2o
  • evict_snapkv
  • gqa
  • linformer
  • lowrank_kv
  • merge_kv
  • mla
  • quantkv

The stored context (μ, k, v) is replaced by something smaller: quantised, low-rank, evicted, merged, or shared across heads. This is the only category that routinely produces value error, because it is the only one that changes what is aggregated.

docs.title: factorize changes the shape of πq4 methods
docs.text:
Changes πq is factored through r latents: πq = a(q, ·) b(·, x). Preserves Row-stochasticity, when both factors are Markov kernels — a composition of two of them is still a probability measure. Error term Distributional, with a floor set by rank. No rank-r factorisation beats the truncated SVD, and a nonnegative one cannot reach it. svd_oracle is that lower bound and nmf_oracle measures the gap. Methods
  • clustered
  • latent_stochastic
  • nmf_oracle
  • svd_oracle

πq is routed through r latents, πq = a(q, ·) b(·, x). Whether the factorisation can stay row-stochastic is the question: latent_stochastic is stochastic by construction, svd_oracle is the signed lower bound it cannot reach, and nmf_oracle measures the gap.

docs.title: coupling changes the normaliser Z2 methods
docs.text:
Changes Normalisation stops being per-query; queries are coupled. Preserves The values, and π̂q as a probability measure. What goes is the independence of the queries, and with it causal masking. Error term Not an approximation error at all. The result is exactly softmax tilted by one potential per key — a deterministic change of operator, measured against softmax only to say how far it has moved. Methods
  • lowrank_ot
  • sinkhorn

Normalisation stops being per-query. Sinkhorn balances the whole matrix to prescribed marginals, which makes the result softmax tilted by a key potential rather than softmax. Queries are no longer independent, so causal masking is not available.

docs.title: recurrent changes the operator itself3 methods
docs.text:
Changes The operator itself becomes a finite-state recurrence. Preserves Linearity in v. That is the whole reason the implied weights can be recovered at all, and why Invariant W still holds here. Error term Not error but capacity. A fixed-size state must answer every future query, which bounds recall however the model is trained. Fidelity to softmax is not the goal, so quoting an output error against it answers a question nobody asked. Methods
  • decay_rnn
  • delta_rnn
  • linear_rnn

The operator becomes a finite-state recurrence: a fixed-size state Ht absorbs the context. Linear in the values, so Invariant W still holds and the implied weights can still be written down — they are simply not a probability measure.

docs.title: The second axis
docs.text:
Cutting across all seven is the question that decides how a method should be judged at all:

objective meaning accelerate the same operator, exact up to floating point approximate targets dense softmax; judged by output error modify a different operator; fidelity to softmax is not the goal

Conflating approximate and modify is the most persistent confusion in this literature. Asking how closely linear_elu approximates softmax is asking the wrong question — it is not trying to. Every method here declares which it is, and the conformance suite uses the declaration: an approximate method must supply a correctness anchor, a modify method is exempt and the suite asserts the exemption rather than skipping it.

docs.title: Reading the columns
docs.text:
declares is three fixed slots, in this order, and a letter struck through is the method declaring no — which on this page is never an omission and always a claim.

w, weights — can the method name its measure \(\widehat\pi_q\) on the original \(n\) positions? A struck-through w means it genuinely cannot, and the method is then excluded from the error-decomposition studies by declaration, not by accident. See the invariant.

s, row-stochastic — are those weights nonnegative and summing to one? nystrom, linformer and the unnormalised recurrences say no, and say it in an attribute rather than in a footnote.

c, causal — a struck-through c is a statement about the operator. Sinkhorn normalises across queries; there is no causal version of that, and asking for one raises an error that says so.

backends — the execution paths this method claims are equal to the reference. Most of the bank is reference only, which is the correct answer for an operator that is not a dense softmax over a mask. See Backends.

docs.title: Oracles
docs.text:
Three methods — value_topk, nmf_oracle, svd_oracle — are not practical. They are upper bounds on what a mechanism can achieve, which is exactly what several of the monograph's arguments need: you cannot show that top-\(k\) selection is suboptimal without computing what the optimal selection would have been.

This page is generated

Everything but the category prose comes from the live registry, so it cannot drift from the code. Regenerate with python docs/gen_taxonomy.py; ab.list_methods() prints the same rows in a terminal. To search and filter the whole bank at once — by category, objective, causal support, backend — use Browse the bank.

docs.title: Conformance (runtime)
docs.text: The design contract as an API, not only as a test file. See the conformance suite for the full eleven points.

docs.title: conformance
docs.text:
Invariant W and the conformance suite, as a runtime API.

The library's one invariant is

y == weights @ (v_hat if v_hat is not None else value)

Every registered method satisfies it, and tests/test_conformance.py proves it in CI over the whole registry in float32 and float64. This module exposes the same checks at runtime, so the guarantee is available to anyone building on top of attnbank:

  • check_invariant -- one output, one number, an exception if it is too large.
  • check_conformance -- one method, a printable report over the checks that can be run quickly; the full eleven-point suite lives in tests/test_conformance.py.

Why it matters: attnbank.metrics splits output error into a distributional term (pi - pi_hat) v and a value term pi_hat (v - v_hat). That split is meaningless unless a method's reported weights and values actually reproduce its output. Invariant W is what makes the decomposition a measurement rather than a story, and it is the reason methods that cannot express their measure on the original n positions declare expresses_weights = False instead of returning something approximate.

Examples:

>>> import torch, attnbank as ab
>>> q, k, v = (torch.randn(1, 2, 8, 16, dtype=torch.float64) for _ in range(3))
>>> out = ab.build("quantkv", bits_k=4, bits_v=4)(q, k, v, return_weights=True)
>>> ab.check_invariant(out, v) < 1e-9
True
>>> print(ab.check_conformance("topk"))
topk: ... checks passed...

def raise_for_status(self) -> "ConformanceReport":
    """Raise :class:`~attnbank.errors.ConformanceError` if anything failed."""
    if not self.ok:
        raise ConformanceError(
            f"{self.name} failed {len(self.failures)} conformance check(s):\n"
            + "\n".join(str(c) for c in self.failures))
    return self

def check_invariant(output: AttentionOutput, value: Optional[Tensor] = None,
                    atol: Optional[float] = None) -> float:
    """Verify ``y == weights @ (v_hat or value)``; return the largest deviation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output:
        an :class:`~attnbank.AttentionOutput` produced with ``return_weights=True``.
    value:
        the ``value`` tensor the method was called with. Required unless the method
        returned ``v_hat`` (in which case ``v_hat`` is the field that was aggregated).
    atol:
        tolerance; defaults to ``1e-10`` in float64 and ``1e-5`` in float32, the
        tolerances in DESIGN.md Sec. 1.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        ``max |y - weights @ v_hat|``, or ``0.0`` when the method declares
        ``expresses_weights = False`` and so returned no weights.

    Raises
    ------
    ~attnbank.errors.ConformanceError
        if the deviation exceeds ``atol``, naming the deviation and the tolerance.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import torch, attnbank as ab
    >>> q, k, v = (torch.randn(1, 1, 6, 4, dtype=torch.float64) for _ in range(3))
    >>> out = ab.build("merge_kv", n_clusters=3)(q, k, v, return_weights=True)
    >>> ab.check_invariant(out, v) < 1e-10
    True
    """
    if output.weights is None:
        return 0.0
    field_ = output.v_hat if output.v_hat is not None else value
    if field_ is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "check_invariant needs the `value` tensor: this output carries weights but "
            "no v_hat, so the aggregated field is the original value. Call "
            "check_invariant(out, value).")
    recon = output.weights @ field_
    dev = float((output.y - recon).abs().max())
    tol = atol if atol is not None else INVARIANT_ATOL.get(output.y.dtype, 1e-5)
    if not dev <= tol:
        raise ConformanceError(
            f"Invariant W violated: max |y - weights @ "
            f"{'v_hat' if output.v_hat is not None else 'value'}| = {dev:.3e} > {tol:.0e}. "
            "Either the weights do not describe what the method aggregated, or the "
            "method should declare expresses_weights = False and return weights=None. "
            "See DESIGN.md Sec. 1.")
    return dev

def check_conformance(name: str, strict: bool = False, **config) -> ConformanceReport:
    """Run the fast half of the conformance suite on one method, right now.

    The checks: output shapes, Invariant W, row stochasticity where declared, causal
    non-leakage, finiteness under large logits, input immutability, reproducibility,
    the cost-model keys, and the exact limit when the method declares one.  The full
    eleven-point suite -- including float64/CUDA agreement, batch and head
    independence, Monte-Carlo convergence and the bibliography check -- is
    ``tests/test_conformance.py``, parametrized over the whole registry.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name:
        a registry key.
    strict:
        raise instead of returning a report with failures.
    **config:
        passed to :func:`attnbank.build`.

    Returns
    -------
    ConformanceReport
        printable; ``report.ok`` is the one-bit answer.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import attnbank as ab
    >>> ab.check_conformance("performer", r=64).ok
    True
    >>> ab.check_conformance("window", w=4).failures
    []
    """
    from .registry import build, get_class

    cls = get_class(name)
    meth = build(name, **config)
    rep = ConformanceReport(name=name, config=dict(config))
    b, h, m, n, d, dv = 2, 2, 6, 12, 8, 6
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    mk = lambda *s: torch.randn(*s, generator=gen, dtype=torch.float64)
    q, k, v = mk(b, h, m, d), mk(b, h, n, d), mk(b, h, n, dv)
    q0, k0, v0 = q.clone(), k.clone(), v.clone()

    out = meth(q, k, v, return_weights=True)

    shapes_ok = (tuple(out.y.shape) == (b, h, m, dv)
                 and (out.weights is None or tuple(out.weights.shape) == (b, h, m, n))
                 and (out.v_hat is None or tuple(out.v_hat.shape) == (b, h, n, dv)))
    rep.checks.append(Check("shapes", shapes_ok, repr(out)))

    if not cls.expresses_weights:
        rep.checks.append(Check("invariant W", None,
                                "expresses_weights = False, by declaration"))
    else:
        try:
            dev = check_invariant(out, v)
            rep.checks.append(Check("invariant W", True, f"max |y - W v| = {dev:.2e}"))
        except ConformanceError as e:
            rep.checks.append(Check("invariant W", False, str(e).split("\n")[0]))

    if cls.row_stochastic and out.weights is not None:
        s = out.weights.sum(-1)
        ok = bool((out.weights >= -1e-12).all()
                  and torch.allclose(s, torch.ones_like(s), atol=1e-9))
        rep.checks.append(Check("row stochastic", ok,
                                f"row sums in [{float(s.min()):.6f}, {float(s.max()):.6f}]"))
    else:
        rep.checks.append(Check("row stochastic", None,
                                "row_stochastic = False, by declaration"))

    if cls.supports_causal:
        base = meth(q, k, v, causal=True).y
        t = n - 2
        k2, v2 = k.clone(), v.clone()
        k2[..., t:, :] += 1.0
        v2[..., t:, :] += 1.0
        pert = meth(q, k2, v2, causal=True).y
        safe = max(0, t - (n - m))
        ok = safe == 0 or bool(torch.equal(base[..., :safe, :], pert[..., :safe, :]))
        rep.checks.append(Check("no causal leakage", ok, f"queries 0..{safe - 1} unchanged"))
    else:
        rep.checks.append(Check("no causal leakage", None,
                                "supports_causal = False, by declaration"))

    big = meth(10.0 * q, 10.0 * k, v, return_weights=True)
    finite = all(t is None or bool(torch.isfinite(t).all())
                 for t in (big.y, big.weights, big.v_hat))
    rep.checks.append(Check("finite at large logits", finite, "q, k scaled by 10"))

    rep.checks.append(Check("inputs not mutated",
                            bool(torch.equal(q, q0) and torch.equal(k, k0)
                                 and torch.equal(v, v0))))

    rep.checks.append(Check("reproducible",
                            bool(torch.equal(build(name, **config)(q, k, v).y,
                                             build(name, **config)(q, k, v).y)),
                            "two builds agree bit for bit"))

    cost = meth.cost(m, n, d, dv)
    cost_ok = (set(cost) == {"flops", "state_bytes", "bytes_moved"}
               and all(c > 0 and c == c and c != float("inf") for c in cost.values()))
    rep.checks.append(Check("cost model", cost_ok, str(cost) if cost_ok else repr(cost)))

    lim = cls.limit_config()
    if lim is not None and not config:
        sq = 12
        qs, ks, vs = mk(b, h, sq, d), mk(b, h, sq, d), mk(b, h, sq, dv)
        got = build(name, **lim)(qs, ks, vs).y
        ref = build("softmax")(qs, ks, vs).y
        err = float((got - ref).abs().max())
        rep.checks.append(Check("exact limit", err <= 1e-5,
                                f"limit_config={lim}, max |y - softmax| = {err:.2e}"))
    elif lim is None and cls.convergence_configs() is not None:
        rep.checks.append(Check("exact limit", None,
                                f"Monte-Carlo: {len(cls.convergence_configs())} "
                                "convergence_configs instead"))
    else:
        rep.checks.append(Check("exact limit", None,
                                "objective = modify; it does not target softmax"
                                if lim is None else "skipped (explicit config given)"))

    return rep.raise_for_status() if strict else rep

docs.title: core
docs.text:
Core interface for attnbank.

Every efficient-attention method is an AttentionMethod. The interface mirrors the paper's framework: attention is y(q) = E_{x ~ pi_q}[v(x)], and a method may change the evaluation (exact), the interaction g, the accessible support, the context representation (mu, k, v), the factorization of pi_q, or the operator.

Tensor convention (all methods): query [B, H, m, d], key [B, H, n, d], value [B, H, n, dv]. Causal masking aligns the last query with the last key (decode-friendly), so m <= n and query i sees keys 0 .. i + (n - m).

The public argument names are query, key, value -- the transformers convention, which also frees k to mean a method's own budget (ab.attend("topk", q, k, v, k=64)). They remain positional, so attn(q, k, v) is unchanged, and the short spellings q=, k=, v= are still accepted as keywords for tensors.

AttentionMethod(
    scale: Optional[float] = None,
    backend: Optional[str] = None,
    **kwargs,

Bases: Module

Base class for every method in the bank.

A subclass declares what it is through class attributes and implements one method, _forward. Everything else -- validation, the causal guard, the registry entry, the conformance suite -- follows from the declaration.

Declaration attributes

name, category, objective, supports_causal, expresses_weights, row_stochastic, head_independent, trainable, references, paper_section. See DESIGN.md Sec. 2 for the exact meaning of each; the conformance suite tests the method against what it declares, so an attribute is a commitment, not documentation.

Examples:

>>> import torch, attnbank as ab
>>> attn = ab.build("topk", k=4)
>>> attn
TopKAttention(name='topk', category='restrict', objective='approximate',
              backend='reference', k=4)
>>> q, k, v = (torch.randn(1, 2, 8, 16) for _ in range(3))
>>> attn(q, k, v, causal=True).y.shape
torch.Size([1, 2, 8, 16])
