docs.title: Nonnegative rank bound
docs.text:
nmf_oracle · ab.build("nmf_oracle")

Oracle — an upper bound, not a method

nmf_oracle is not deployable and is not meant to be. It uses information no inference-time method has, and it is in the bank to answer how well could this ever work? — several of the monograph's arguments need that number. Read every result below as a bound on a family of real methods, never as a baseline you could ship.

Nonnegative rank bound: the best rank-r nonnegative factorization of P.

category factorize — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.NMFOracleAttention, attnbank/methods/factorize/nmf_oracle.py monograph sec:factor

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the shape of \(\pi_q\): it is routed through \(r\) latents, \(\pi_q = a(q,\cdot)\,b(\cdot,x)\), which caps the rank of the attention matrix at \(r\).

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:factor-rank, prop:factor-rank. For a row-stochastic P the hierarchy is

rank(P) <= rank_+(P) = rank_s(P),

so the smallest rank of a stochastic factorization equals the nonnegative rank, and stochastic factorization is NMF with a free renormalization. This file is the empirical side of that statement: it fits P ~ W H with W, H >= 0 of inner dimension r by Lee–Seung multiplicative updates on the Frobenius loss,

W <- W * (P H^T) / (W H H^T),     H <- H * (W^T P) / (W^T W H),

from restarts seeded initializations, keeping the best, and then renormalizes the rows of W H so the result is a genuine row-stochastic P_hat — legitimate by the rescaling argument in the proof of prop:factor-rank. The unnormalized product and its Frobenius residual are returned in extras so that the fit quality can be separated from the renormalization.

This is an oracle, not a method anyone deploys: it gives the best a nonnegative rank-r factorization could do, so that the gap against svd_oracle — which has no nonnegativity constraint and is optimal by Eckart–Young — measures the nonnegative-rank penalty that every stochastic latent attention pays. Multiplicative updates converge to a stationary point, not a global optimum, so the gap it reports is an upper bound on the true penalty.

Exact limit: r = None returns W = P, H = I — the exact nonnegative factorization of rank n.

Not causal: a nonnegative factorization of a masked P only approximates the zeros.

docs.title: Nystromformer
docs.text:
nystrom · ab.build("nystrom")

Nystromformer: landmark Nystrom approximation of the row-stochastic matrix.

category interaction — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.NystromAttention, attnbank/methods/interaction/nystrom.py monograph sec:kernel

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the interaction \(g(q,x)\), replaced by a surrogate \(\widehat g\). \(\pi_q = \widehat g(q,\cdot)\mu / \widehat Z(q)\) is then a different measure on the same \(n\) positions.

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:kernel-matrix and sec:factor-methods. With r landmark queries and keys obtained by segment means of Q and K,

P_hat = softmax(beta Q Kt^T) * G^+ * softmax(beta Qt K^T),
G     = softmax(beta Qt Kt^T),

where Qt, Kt are the landmarks and G^+ the pseudo-inverse (the original uses an iterative approximation of it; this reference implementation uses an exact pinv in float64, so that the only error measured is the method's, not the solver's).

Three caveats the paper makes and this file honours.

  1. P is neither symmetric nor PSD when Q != K, so Nystrom theory does not apply; there is no spectral guarantee here.

  2. The pseudo-inverse makes P_hat signed: pi_hat is a signed measure of unit mass, so the contract items nm and hl are lost — row_stochastic is False, and outputs can leave the convex hull of the values. (Rows do sum to one when G is invertible, since G^{-1} 1 = 1 for a stochastic G; the library does not rely on that.)

  3. Segment-mean landmarks summarize the context, so the method also modifies mu.

Exact limit. With r = None the landmarks are the data themselves (Qt = Q, Kt = K, which requires m = n), giving P_hat = P P^+ P = P exactly by the Moore–Penrose identity. That is the correctness anchor.

Not causal: the segment means pool over the whole sequence.

docs.title: What it declares
docs.text:
Each row is a commitment the conformance suite tests, not a description.

attribute declared what that commits it to supports_causal no causal=True raises CausalNotSupportedError — a statement about the operator, not a missing feature. expresses_weights yes it can name \(\widehat\pi_q\) on the original \(n\) positions, so it enters the error decomposition. row_stochastic no the weights are not a probability measure — signed, or not summing to one — so the output can leave the convex hull of the values. head_independent yes each head is computed from its own \(K, V\). trainable no no learned parameters — what you build is what the paper describes.

docs.title: Cost model
docs.text:
Analytic, per (batch, head), declared by the method itself:

def cost(self, m, n, d, dv, bytes_per_el=2):
    r = self.r or min(m, n)
    return {"flops": 2 * (m + n) * r * d + 2 * r ** 3 + 2 * (m + n) * r * dv,
            "state_bytes": r * (d + dv) * bytes_per_el,
            "bytes_moved": (m * d + n * (d + dv) + m * dv + r * (d + dv)) * bytes_per_el}

At \(m = 1024\), \(n = 1024\), \(d = 64\), \(dv = 64\) and bytes_per_el=2, against the reference operator at the same shape:

quantity this method softmax ratio flops 8,396,800 268,435,456 0.0313× state_bytes 4,096 262,144 0.0156× bytes_moved 528,384 4,718,592 0.112×

A cost model is not a benchmark

These are counted operations and resident bytes, not measured time. They are what the monograph's capacity arguments are made of; examples/08_cost_and_capacity.py walks through the comparison properly.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
import torch, attnbank as ab

torch.manual_seed(0)
b, h, n, d = 1, 2, 64, 32
q, k, v = (torch.randn(b, h, n, d) for _ in range(3))

attn = ab.build("nystrom", r=16)
out = attn(q, k, v, causal=False,   # it declares supports_causal = False
           return_weights=True)

print(attn)
print(out)
print("invariant W:", out.check_invariant(v))

# objective = approximate: it targets dense softmax, so it is judged by
# output error -- split into the distributional and value terms.
row = ab.compare(["nystrom"], q, k, v, causal=False,
                 configs={"nystrom": {'r': 16}})[0]
print({key: round(row[key], 5) for key in
       ("output_error", "distributional_error", "value_error", "tv")})

docs.title: Performer / FAVOR+
docs.text:
performer · ab.build("performer")

Performer / FAVOR+: positive random features for the exponential kernel.

category interaction — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.PerformerAttention, attnbank/methods/interaction/performer.py monograph sec:kernel

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the interaction \(g(q,x)\), replaced by a surrogate \(\widehat g\). \(\pi_q = \widehat g(q,\cdot)\mu / \widehat Z(q)\) is then a different measure on the same \(n\) positions.

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:kernel-rf. With qt = q / d^{1/4} and kt = k / d^{1/4} the softmax interaction is g(q,x) = exp(<qt, kt_x>) and FAVOR+ uses the positive, unbiased estimator

phi_omega(u) = exp(omega^T u - ||u||^2 / 2),
g_hat(q,x)   = (1/r) sum_{l=1}^r phi_{omega_l}(qt) phi_{omega_l}(kt_x),
omega_l ~ N(0, I_d)   i.i.d. or exactly orthogonal in blocks of d.

Because phi >= 0 the normalizer Z_hat > 0 and pi_hat is a genuine probability measure (prop:error-additive: positivity is essential). The relative variance at a pair is (exp(||qt + kt||^2) - 1) / r (eq:kernel-pos-var), so the cost of a fixed accuracy is exponential in the squared logit scale.

The output is a ratio of two unbiased estimators, so it is itself biased: prop:error-ratio-est gives bias O(1/r) and standard deviation O(r^{-1/2}). convergence_configs exists for exactly this reason — there is no finite r at which the method is exact.

Implementation note. The sum over features is evaluated as a log-sum-exp rather than as the O(nr) moment product, because the library needs pi_hat on the original positions and because phi is bounded above by exp(||omega||^2/2) but can underflow to zero in the tail. The value computed is the same estimator.

docs.title: KV-cache quantization
docs.text:
quantkv · ab.build("quantkv")

KV-cache quantization: uniform affine (asymmetric) quantization of keys and values.

category compress — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.QuantKVAttention, attnbank/methods/compress/quantkv.py monograph sec:compress

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the stored context \((\mu, k, v)\) itself. This is the one category that routinely perturbs the integrand, so \(\widehat v \neq v\) and the error has a value term.

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:compress-quant and prop:compress-sensitivity. Keys and values stay on the same domain; only their representation changes, so

k_hat_j = Q_{b_k}(k_j),   v_hat_j = Q_{b_v}(v_j),
Q_b(x)  = round((x - lo) / Delta) * Delta + lo,   Delta = (hi - lo) / (2^b - 1),

with lo, hi the min and max over a group. The key error enters as a log-weight perturbation delta_l_j = beta <q, delta k_j> — an exponential tilt of pi_q — and is amplified by e^{osc(delta_l)} - 1 and by ||q||; the value error enters linearly and is attention-weighted. That asymmetry is the content of prop:compress-sensitivity and of eq:error-joint, and is what study S4 measures.

Grouping. axis='token' shares a scale among group channels of one token (KIVI's value grouping); axis='channel' shares it among group tokens of one channel (KIVI's key grouping, which confines an outlier channel's coarse step to that channel). Only the token-varying part of the key error matters, since softmax cancels a common shift — which is exactly why per-channel grouping helps for keys.

Per-channel grouping pools statistics across tokens, so it is not causal; the method raises rather than silently leaking. axis='token' is causal and is the default.

Exact limit: bits_k = bits_v = None (the identity quantizer). 16-bit affine quantization is not bit-exact in fp32, so it would be a dishonest anchor.

The quantizer itself is attnbank.components.quantization.affine_quantize, shared with lowprec; this file is only the decision to apply it to the cache.

docs.title: Cost model
docs.text:
Analytic, per (batch, head), declared by the method itself:

def cost(self, m, n, d, dv, bytes_per_el=2):
    bk = (self.bits_k or 8 * bytes_per_el) / 8
    bv = (self.bits_v or 8 * bytes_per_el) / 8
    state = n * (d * bk + dv * bv)
    return {"flops": 2 * m * n * (d + dv), "state_bytes": state,
            "bytes_moved": m * (d + dv) * bytes_per_el + state}

At \(m = 1024\), \(n = 1024\), \(d = 64\), \(dv = 64\) and bytes_per_el=2, against the reference operator at the same shape:

docs.title: StreamingLLM
docs.text:
sink_window · ab.build("sink_window")

StreamingLLM: the first s "attention sink" positions plus a sliding window.

category restrict — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.SinkWindowAttention, attnbank/methods/restrict/sink_window.py monograph sec:sparse

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the support of \(\pi_q\), which shrinks to \(S_q \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}\) and is renormalised on it. The values \(v\) are untouched, so the whole error is distributional.

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:sparse-fixed, sec:compress-evict, ex:sparse-sink. The support is {0, ..., s-1} union {p-w+1, ..., p}: content-independent, and therefore an eviction policy as much as a sparsity pattern.

The reason it works is prop:sparse-identity read backwards. A head that routes mass eps to a sink with a near-null value computes y = (1-eps) m_S; a pure window outputs m_S, an amplification by 1/(1-eps). Retaining the sink restores the normalizer, not information: the sink carries normalization. Comparing sink_window(s>0) with window at the same total budget isolates that effect, which is what makes the pair worth having in the library.

            "bytes_moved": (m * d + m * kept * (d + dv) + m * dv) * bytes_per_el}

docs.title: Sinkhorn / entropic-OT attention
docs.text:
sinkhorn · ab.build("sinkhorn")

Sinkhorn / entropic-OT attention: prescribe the column marginal too.

category coupling — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective modify — defines a different operator; fidelity to softmax is not the goal class attnbank.SinkhornAttention, attnbank/methods/coupling/sinkhorn.py monograph sec:ot

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the normalisation. \(Z(q)\) stops being a per-query constant and becomes a global constraint, so the queries are no longer independent of one another.

It pursues modification: it defines a different operator. Asking how closely it approximates softmax is asking the wrong question — it is not trying to.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:ot-eot. Softmax attention is semi-relaxed entropic OT: it minimizes int c dgamma + eps KL(gamma || nu x mubar) subject to the row marginal only (prop:ot-gibbs). Adding the column constraint gives entropic OT, and the central structural fact (prop:ot-conditional) is that its conditionals are still softmax — tilted by a query-independent key potential:

pi^OT_q(dx) ∝ exp( beta ( <q, k_x> + psi(x) ) ) mubar(dx).

So a doubly stochastic attention operator is characterised, completely, by one vector psi per context: an economic price that is negative on keys over-subscribed under softmax and positive on under-subscribed ones. extras["potential"] returns the quantity psi in the form in which the identity can be checked directly, pi_hat = softmax_j(s_ij / eps + potential_j), which is what study S7 does.

Sinkhorn's algorithm alternates the two identities of prop:ot-conditional (b) in log domain (eq:ot-sinkhorn): a row log-sum-exp (a softmax normalizer) followed by a column log-sum-exp. One step from psi = 0, stopped after the row update, is exactly softmax attention — so n_iter = 0 is the exact limit, and the whole operator family is a continuation of softmax in the number of iterations.

Not causal, and not by omission: prop:ot-causal shows that a lower-triangular matrix with equal row and column sums is diagonal. Causal attention with uniform marginals is the identity, every token attending only to itself. A non-uniform column marginal satisfying sum_{j>=t} b_j <= sum_{i>=t} a_i is the way out, and is not implemented here.

docs.title: What it declares
docs.text:
Each row is a commitment the conformance suite tests, not a description.

attribute declared what that commits it to supports_causal no causal=True raises CausalNotSupportedError — a statement about the operator, not a missing feature. expresses_weights yes it can name \(\widehat\pi_q\) on the original \(n\) positions, so it enters the error decomposition. row_stochastic yes those weights are \(\ge 0\) and sum to one: \(\widehat\pi_q\) is a probability measure. head_independent yes each head is computed from its own \(K, V\). trainable no no learned parameters — what you build is what the paper describes.

docs.text:
backend what it is reference plain PyTorch; the correctness anchor and the default

reference only, and that is the correct answer. A fixed-point iteration over the whole matrix is not a kernel call, and the normalisation it computes is not per-query.

Declaring a backend is a claim that it equals the reference, checked by tests/test_conformance.py::test_backend_equivalence; declaring sdpa here would be pretending. See Backends.

docs.title: Cost model
docs.text:
Analytic, per (batch, head), declared by the method itself:

def cost(self, m, n, d, dv, bytes_per_el=2):
    return {"flops": 2 * m * n * (d + dv) + 2 * self.n_iter * m * n,
            "state_bytes": n * (d + dv) * bytes_per_el + n * 4,   # + the key potential
            "bytes_moved": (m * d + n * (d + dv) + m * dv
                            + 2 * self.n_iter * m * n) * bytes_per_el}

At \(m = 1024\), \(n = 1024\), \(d = 64\), \(dv = 64\) and bytes_per_el=2, against the reference operator at the same shape:

quantity this method softmax ratio flops 278,921,216 268,435,456 1.04× state_bytes 266,240 262,144 1.02× bytes_moved 21,495,808 4,718,592 4.56×

A cost model is not a benchmark

These are counted operations and resident bytes, not measured time. They are what the monograph's capacity arguments are made of; examples/08_cost_and_capacity.py walks through the comparison properly.

b, h, n, d = 1, 2, 64, 32

attn = ab.build("sinkhorn", n_iter=5, eps=1.0)
out = attn(q, k, v, causal=False,   # it declares supports_causal = False

      [round(x, 4) for x in out.weights.sum(-1)[0, 0, :4].tolist()])

docs.title: Signed rank bound
docs.text:
svd_oracle · ab.build("svd_oracle")

Oracle — an upper bound, not a method

svd_oracle is not deployable and is not meant to be. It uses information no inference-time method has, and it is in the bank to answer how well could this ever work? — several of the monograph's arguments need that number. Read every result below as a bound on a family of real methods, never as a baseline you could ship.

Signed rank bound: the best rank-r signed factorization of P (truncated SVD).

category factorize — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.SVDOracleAttention, attnbank/methods/factorize/svd_oracle.py monograph sec:factor

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the shape of \(\pi_q\): it is routed through \(r\) latents, \(\pi_q = a(q,\cdot)\,b(\cdot,x)\), which caps the rank of the attention matrix at \(r\).

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:factor-rank. The truncated SVD P_r = U_r Sigma_r V_r^T is the optimal rank-r approximation of P in every unitarily invariant norm (Eckart–Young), so it is the lower bound that no stochastic factorization of the same rank can beat: rank(P) <= rank_+(P) = rank_s(P), and the inequality is usually strict. The gap between this file and nmf_oracle is the empirical nonnegative-rank penalty of study S5.

The price of optimality is the whole contract: P_r is signed, its rows do not sum to one, and the output can leave the convex hull of the values — exactly the failure mode prop:factor-closure was stated to rule out for Markov compositions. row_stochastic = False records it; the row sums and the most negative weight are returned in extras so the violation can be measured instead of assumed.

This is an oracle: no one computes a per-head SVD of P at inference. It exists to bound what any rank-r method could achieve. The decomposition is taken in float64.

Exact limit: r = None keeps the full spectrum. Not causal: the truncation does not preserve the mask's zeros.

docs.title: What it declares
docs.text:
Each row is a commitment the conformance suite tests, not a description.

attribute declared what that commits it to supports_causal no causal=True raises CausalNotSupportedError — a statement about the operator, not a missing feature. expresses_weights yes it can name \(\widehat\pi_q\) on the original \(n\) positions, so it enters the error decomposition. row_stochastic no the weights are not a probability measure — signed, or not summing to one — so the output can leave the convex hull of the values. head_independent yes each head is computed from its own \(K, V\). trainable no no learned parameters — what you build is what the paper describes.

            "state_bytes": r * n * bytes_per_el,
            "bytes_moved": (m * d + n * (d + dv) + m * dv) * bytes_per_el}

docs.text:
topk · ab.build("topk")

Oracle top-k restriction: the k largest true scores, renormalized.

category restrict — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.TopKAttention, attnbank/methods/restrict/topk.py monograph sec:sparse

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the support of \(\pi_q\), which shrinks to \(S_q \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}\) and is renormalised on it. The values \(v\) are untouched, so the whole error is distributional.

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:sparse-operator, sec:sparse-query. S_q is the set of the k largest exact attention weights, which by prop:error-topk minimizes the omitted mass eps_q — and hence the bound eps_q osc(v) — over all supports of size k. It is the oracle against which every proxy selector (Quest, SparQ, Loki, H2O) is measured: computing all scores saves only the value aggregation.

The proposition's second half matters more for this library: minimizing eps_q is not minimizing ||y - y_hat||. With pi = (0.45, 0.35, 0.20) and scalar values (0, 0, 1), top-2 retains {1,2} and errs by 0.2 while {1,3} omits more mass and errs by 0.11. value_topk is the output-aware alternative; the gap between them is the quantity study S2 reports.

docs.title: Random Fourier features for attention
docs.text:
trigrff · ab.build("trigrff")

Random Fourier features for attention: the trigonometric (signed) estimator.

category interaction — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.TrigRFFAttention, attnbank/methods/interaction/trigrff.py monograph sec:kernel

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the interaction \(g(q,x)\), replaced by a surrogate \(\widehat g\). \(\pi_q = \widehat g(q,\cdot)\mu / \widehat Z(q)\) is then a different measure on the same \(n\) positions.

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:kernel-rf. Bochner's theorem for the Gaussian kernel plus eq:kernel-softmax-gauss gives the unbiased estimator

xi_omega(q,x) = exp((||qt||^2 + ||kt_x||^2)/2) * cos(omega^T (qt - kt_x)),
omega ~ N(0, I_d),   qt = q/d^{1/4},  kt = k/d^{1/4},

separable with 2r features through cos(a-b) = cos a cos b + sin a sin b. This is the basis of RFA (Peng et al., 2021) and of the trigonometric variant of Choromanski et al. (2021).

Two things go wrong, and this file exists so that they can be measured. (i) The relative variance is 2 sinh^2(||qt - kt_x||^2 / 2) (eq:kernel-trig-var), largest for keys far from the query — the many small entries whose accumulated noise makes Z_hat unreliable. (ii) xi takes both signs, so Z_hat can be zero or negative; then pi_hat is not a probability measure and no bound of the form prop:error-additive holds. The fraction of queries with Z_hat <= 0 is reported in extras["Z_rel"].

Numerics. The factor exp(||kt_j||^2/2) does not cancel in pi_hat and overflows fp32 for large inputs, so the estimator is carried as a (log-magnitude, sign) pair and normalized by attnbank.weights_from_log_magnitude, which subtracts the maximum over the visible keys. When |Z_hat| is below the floor the result is finite but large; this is a reported failure, not a silent repair.

docs.title: Output-aware selection
docs.text:
value_topk · ab.build("value_topk")

Oracle — an upper bound, not a method

value_topk is not deployable and is not meant to be. It uses information no inference-time method has, and it is in the bank to answer how well could this ever work? — several of the monograph's arguments need that number. Read every result below as a bound on a family of real methods, never as a baseline you could ship.

Output-aware selection: the support that minimizes output error, chosen greedily.

category restrict — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.ValueTopKAttention, attnbank/methods/restrict/value_topk.py monograph sec:sparse

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
Changes the support of \(\pi_q\), which shrinks to \(S_q \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}\) and is renormalised on it. The values \(v\) are untouched, so the whole error is distributional.

It pursues approximation: it is trying to be dense softmax, so it is fair to judge it by output error, and it must supply a correctness anchor saying where it becomes exact.

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:sparse-operator ("Score-optimal is not output-optimal"), prop:error-topk, and the open problem of sec:open-retrieval. Top-k minimizes the omitted mass eps_q and therefore the bound eps_q osc(v); it does not minimize the error. The right target, named in the text, is

min_{|S| <= k}  eps_S ||m_{S^c} - m_S||.

That objective simplifies. For a renormalized restriction y_hat = m_S, so with W_S = pi(S) and U_S = sum_{j in S} pi_j v_j,

eps_S ||m_{S^c} - m_S|| = ||y - m_S|| = ||y - U_S / W_S||,

i.e. the objective is just the realised output error, and no conditional mean of the complement needs to be formed.

Selection. Forward greedy alone is badly myopic here: its first pick minimizes ||y - v_j|| and so can seed the support with a light outlier that later additions cannot undo. The selector therefore evaluates four cheap candidate supports and keeps, per query, whichever realises the smallest error:

  1. score top-k (so the result is never worse than topk, by construction);
  2. forward greedy from the empty set;
  3. forward greedy seeded with the single heaviest position;
  4. backward greedy from the full set, deleting the position whose removal costs least — the elementary step of every eviction policy, and exactly prop:error-single.

Complexity. Each greedy step scores all n candidates, and a candidate is scored in O(d_v) from the running (U_S, W_S) rather than by recomputing the conditional mean, so a forward pass is O(n k d_v) per query and the backward pass O(n (n - k) d_v) — the naive form of either is O(n^2 k). All queries are processed in parallel, at a peak memory of B H m n d_v; pass chunk to process the query axis in slices if that is too large.

None of this is optimal: exhaustive=True enumerates every support of size k (guarded by max_subsets) and gives the true minimum, which is what tests/test_restrict.py uses to bound the greedy gap.

This is an oracle: it reads v and the exact pi_q, which no deployed selector can. Its purpose is to upper-bound what output-aware selection could buy, so correctness matters and speed does not.

category restrict — one of the seven objects in \(y(q)=\int v\,\mathrm{d}\pi_q\) a method can change objective approximate — targets fidelity to dense softmax; judged by output error class attnbank.WindowAttention, attnbank/methods/restrict/window.py monograph sec:sparse

docs.title: In the paper's notation
docs.text:
sec:sparse-fixed. Query at absolute position p attends to {p - w + 1, ..., p}, intersected with what the mask allows. The diagonal is always included, so no row is ever empty.

Applied to a dense-trained model this is an approximation whose error is exactly eps_q (m_{S^c} - m_S) (prop:sparse-identity); it is the cleanest demonstration of the sink effect of ex:sparse-sink, because once the window has scrolled past position 0 it omits a large mass whose conditional mean is the sink value, and renormalization inflates the remaining weights by 1/(1 - eps_q). Compare with sink_window, which differs only by the first s positions.
